title: History: similar graphs can accompany different selected years
legend: Qwen3-4B attribution graphs for 16 historical-date prompts, including 11 correct and five incorrect predictions. **a,** Two real pairs asking for the year of adoption of the US Declaration of Independence. Within each row, the dates assigned to A and B are swapped while the question and context remain unchanged. When the question comes first, the model predicts A in both prompts, selecting 1776 in one and 1783 in the other; feature overlap is 0.795. When context comes first, the model changes from A to B to retain the correct year, 1776; overlap is 0.512. The exact user-prompt text is shown with added line breaks; the model chat wrapper is not shown. **b,** All eight comparisons that swap the A/B date assignments while holding the queried event and question/context order fixed. The five same-letter comparisons select different years, with one correct and one incorrect prediction per pair (Jaccard 0.795–0.911). The three different-letter comparisons retain the same correct year (0.512–0.532). **c,** All eight comparisons that reverse question/context order while holding the event and A/B date assignments fixed. Overlap is 0.766–0.808 when predictions retain the same letter and 0.527–0.602 when the letter changes. Each point represents a pair of graphs; marker shapes and colors identify the queried event. Panels b and c reuse the same 16 graphs from two event pairs. Jaccard overlap is the number of shared feature identities divided by the number present in either graph; 0 means none are shared and 1 means the feature sets are identical. Feature identities exclude embeddings, output nodes, and reconstruction-error nodes. The panels report descriptive comparisons without treating graph pairs as independent replications.
